migration_recommendation.strategy: PER-CATEGORY, 3 batches (buildings, then land_units, then verify). NOT one 1837-file atomic batch.
migration_recommendation.why: world.gd _sheet() checks subfolders first and still falls back to root, so any partial move is runtime-safe; per-category allows verification after each step and small rollback units. Naval is already migrated and is the working reference.
steps: 0. Freeze: commit current work or create a worktree; record git diff of all .import files; copy this manifest.
2. Batch A - buildings: for each of the 1525 PNGs, os.replace PNG and .png.import into buildings/; rewrite the 3 import fields using manifest hashes.
3. Verify A: count buildings/*.png == 1525 and .import == 1525; sample-check source_file + hash; run godot --headless --path app --editor --quit; run building render tests.
4. Batch B - land_units: same for 312 PNGs + imports.
5. Verify B: count land_units/*.png == 312; run t-anim-metrics, mill_visual_test (after path fix), unit-draw smoke test.
6. Patch REQUIRED tools/tests listed in code_references (before step 3 if regeneration may occur).
7. Final: root should contain only 4 JSONs, naval/, the two new subfolders and empty tmp/. git add -A to record renames.
migration_recommendation.mechanics: Prefer Python os.replace + in-place .import rewrite driven by this manifest (single deterministic pass, gives inverse list). git mv alone preserves rename detection but will NOT rewrite .import internals; if using git mv, follow with the same .import rewrite step.
migration_recommendation.rollback: For each applied entry, os.replace target/PNG and target/PNG.import back to root, restore original .import text from saved diff, then rmdir empty subfolders. Do not use git checkout because of pre-existing uncommitted changes.
